parsed.explanation: Combined regime: this division has no bathroom ban, no sex-definition law, and a low-risk assessment, with gubernatorial vetoes and patchwork local protections, but federal rules do not cancel. Federal screening instructs refusal on document discrepancy/doubt and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal single-sex facilities are barred by executive order, and national custody records document forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Youth care paused under federal funding pressure despite state vetoes. Courts have blocked some orders, yet passport and health challenges remain unresolved and hate-crime/anti-discrimination cover is incomplete.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal cable requires refusal and more evidence where documents/records diverge or doubt sex; suspected wilful misrepresentation may be considered for permanent fraud ineligibility. X-marker passports no longer processed; confiscations/blocking reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry. Division has no law defining sex to exclude trans people.
entry_documents.interaction: State tolerance does not cancel federal border screening; discrepancy can escalate from secondary inspection to refusal/fraud consideration.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policies from 2026 mandate hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several federal orders blocked/enjoined; no division bathroom-arrest law documented. No visitor-specific release remedy documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border or facility encounter leading to detention exposes traveller to national custody practices regardless of state law.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity, a universal exposure in federal buildings.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division has no ban on using government bathrooms consistent with identity; 2019 executive order bars gender-identity discrimination in state services.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State non-ban protects state buildings, but federal buildings follow the federal bar; traveller must navigate both regimes.

care_services.exposure: Two major hospital systems paused gender-affirming pharmacologic care under 18 in January 2026 after federal payment denial threat; proposed federal rules would bar public-insurance reimbursement.
care_services.protection: Division has no minor care ban; governor vetoed bans in 2023; mental-health services continued; state attorney general joined coalition against federal declaration.
care_services.interaction: Federal funding pressure operated despite state vetoes, affecting travelling minors; adult care continuity for visitors is not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender; justice guidance invokes radical gender ideology; orders direct investigation of schools for gender ideology.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Governor made pro-inclusion statements and vetoed restrictive bills; courts have enjoined several orders.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal threat framing can inform officer discretion at borders/facilities despite division's inclusionary executive posture.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal orders direct criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition and subpoenaed hospital records for under-19 patients; youth pharmacologic care paused at two systems.
minors_guardians.protection: Division enacted no care or sports ban; legislature-passed bans vetoed 2023-2024, athletic associations retained policies.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor faces federal care/education pressure and state legislative risk contained only by veto, with unresolved federal challenges.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Gender identity is not a hate-crime protected class in the division and no statewide anti-discrimination law exists; prosecutors sometimes route via perceived sexual orientation, systematic use not documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Sexual orientation is protected in hate-crime law; 21% lived in cities with full identity ordinances and 12% partial as of May 2025.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Patchwork local ordinances create uneven police/court recourse; no division-specific trans violence rate is documented.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No statewide gender-identity anti-discrimination or hate-crime protection; passport-marker suit and federal health challenges unresolved; remedy for visitors detained or refused not documented.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2019 state executive order covers state employment, contracting and services; some federal orders blocked; legal-aid FAQ on passport rules exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper and partial protections reduce but do not remove federal exposure; effectiveness depends on which orders are in force at travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Case sits well above 0.15: no systematic arrests for presentation, months-long custody before trial, or state-tolerated beatings for visitors are documented in this division. Federal custody abuse is severe, but imprisonment for being trans is not shown as routine or highly likely.

Similar to 0.55-B: extended secondary screening, discretionary refusal and slow remedies are central. Case is lower because federal facility exclusion, lifetime-ineligibility consideration and documented custody abuse add severity beyond administrative delay alone.

Case is materially below 0.85: unlike explicit nationwide equality protections with independent audits and discipline, this regime has federal document/facility restrictions, no statewide GI protection, patchwork ordinances, and unresolved litigation, so remedies cannot be assumed to work.

parsed.synthesis: State-level absence of bans and veto history soften exposure in state buildings and services, but do not neutralise federal entry screening, federal facilities, federal custody and funding pressure. The operative risk is document discrepancy leading to refusal or fraud consideration, federal facility exclusion, and severe harm if detained, tempered by courts enjoining some orders and patchwork local recourse. For families, paused youth pharmacologic care under federal pressure is an additional traveller-facing exposure.
